answer:
Model air as an ideal gas with γ = 1.4 undergoing steady, isentropic, quasi-one-dimensional flow through a converging nozzle with constant stagnation temperature.
Set inlet conditions: M₁ = 2.0 (supersonic inlet).
Set nozzle geometry: converging area ratio A₂/A₁ = 0.7 (so A₂ < A₁).
Determine the critical area A* from the inlet conditions by evaluating the isentropic area-Mach relation A₁/A* = f(M₁, γ) on the supersonic branch.
Compute A₂/A* = (A₂/A₁) × (A₁/A*).
Solve the isentropic area-Mach relation A₂/A* = f(M₂, γ) on the supersonic branch (M₂ > 1) to find M₂. Note that because A decreases in supersonic flow, M₂ < M₁, so the flow decelerates.
Compute the speed of sound at inlet: a₁ = √(γ R T₁), and at exit: a₂ = √(γ R T₂), where T₂ is obtained from the isentropic relation T₀/T = 1 + ((γ−1)/2) M² with T₀ constant.
Compute inlet velocity V₁ = M₁ · a₁ and exit velocity V₂ = M₂ · a₂.
Report the change in velocity ΔV = V₂ − V₁, which will be negative (deceleration), and also report the percentage change ΔV/V₁.
Note explicitly that the problem title's wording "increase in exit velocity" is misleading; the physically correct result is a decrease in velocity due to the supersonic branch of the area-Mach relation in a converging nozzle.
